steps.body: Meet the parent: f(x) = 1/x. Two sweeping branches — first and third quadrants — that **hug two lines without ever touching them**: the vertical line x = 0 (banned input) and the horizontal line y = 0 (unreachable output). Those lines are the **asymptotes**.
Magnify the reciprocal at the one place it refuses to exist.

widget.prompt: y = 1/x² near x = 0. Magnify and decide whether the y-values settle on any number.
widget.successFeedback: They never settle — the closer you look, the larger they grow. A vertical asymptote is not a value the function reaches; it is a place where the function has no value AND no limit, and no magnification will repair it.
widget.moreZoomFeedback: Keep magnifying. A limit that exists gets EASIER to read as you zoom; this one gets worse, and that is the diagnosis.
widget.wrongVerdictFeedback: 'Goes to infinity' describes how the limit fails, not a number it approaches. The y-values never settle, so there is no limit here.

predict.prompt: You'll zoom in at x = 0. What will the two sides of the graph do?

options.label: Close in on the same height

predict.reveal: Zooming never tames it — the graph climbs off every window near x = 0. When the values grow without bound, there is no height to agree on, so the limit does not exist.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents rf reciprocal.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for rf reciprocal must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines rf reciprocal.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: Near x = 0 the outputs explode (1/0.001 = 1000); far away they flatten (1/1000 = 0.001, never reaching 0 exactly). Transformations move the whole picture: f(x) = 1/(x − 2) + 1 slides the asymptote pair to **x = 2 and y = 1** — the branches follow their guide rails.

explanationVariants: 1/x = 0 would need a numerator of 0 — but the top is fixed at 1: no input works.
A fraction is zero only when its TOP is zero; this top never is.

options.label: a fraction equals 0 only when its numerator does — and this one is always 1
options.feedback: Right — solve 1/x = 0: no x can make it true.

options.label: because x = 0 is excluded
options.feedback: That explains the VERTICAL asymptote (banned input) — the unreachable OUTPUT is about the numerator staying 1.

options.label: it does, at very large x
options.feedback: 1/1000000 is tiny but still positive — flattening toward 0 is not reaching 0.

options.label: because 1/x is always positive
options.feedback: 1/(−2) = −½ is negative — the third-quadrant branch exists; it's exactly 0 that's impossible.

widget.prompt: Where are the asymptotes of g(x) = 1/(x − 2) + 1?

options.label: x = 2 and y = 1
options.feedback: Right — the denominator dies at 2; the +1 lifts the horizontal rail.

options.label: x = −2 and y = 1
options.feedback: Inside shifts oppose their sign: x − 2 dies at POSITIVE 2.

options.label: x = 2 and y = −1
options.feedback: The +1 is outside and as-written: the horizontal asymptote RISES to y = 1.

options.label: x = 1 and y = 2
options.feedback: Vertical comes from the DENOMINATOR (x = 2); horizontal from the outside shift (y = 1) — don't swap.

explanationVariants: Just right of 2, the denominator x − 2 is tiny and positive: 1/(tiny+) is huge and positive — up the wall.

widget.prompt: As x approaches 2 from the RIGHT, what does g(x) = 1/(x − 2) + 1 do?

options.label: shoots up toward +∞
options.feedback: Right — a tiny POSITIVE denominator makes the fraction enormous and positive.

options.label: shoots down toward −∞
options.feedback: From the right, x − 2 is a tiny POSITIVE number — the fraction blows up UPWARD (down happens from the left).

options.label: levels off at y = 1
options.feedback: Leveling at y = 1 happens FAR from the wall (large x) — near x = 2 the fraction dominates.

options.label: approaches g(2)
options.feedback: g(2) doesn't exist — 2 is the banned input; the graph climbs the asymptote instead.

explanationVariants: Every output except 0 is achieved: y = 5 at x = 1/5, y = −3 at x = −1/3 — only 0 is impossible.
Solve 1/x = k: x = 1/k works for every k ≠ 0.

widget.prompt: What is the RANGE of f(x) = 1/x?

options.label: all real numbers except 0
options.feedback: Right — for any k ≠ 0, x = 1/k lands exactly on it.

options.label: all real numbers
options.feedback: 0 is the one impossible output — the numerator can never vanish.

options.label: y > 0
options.feedback: Negative inputs give negative outputs: f(−2) = −½ — the third-quadrant branch is real.

options.label: y ≠ 1
options.feedback: f(1) = 1 works fine — the unreachable value is 0, the horizontal asymptote.

explanationVariants: h(x) = 1/(x + 3) − 2: denominator dies at −3 (vertical); the −2 drops the horizontal rail to y = −2.
Asymptotes move with the shifts: left 3, down 2.

widget.prompt: Where are the asymptotes of h(x) = 1/(x + 3) − 2?

options.label: x = −3 and y = −2
options.feedback: Right — inside shift left 3, outside shift down 2.

options.label: x = 3 and y = −2
options.feedback: x + 3 = 0 at NEGATIVE 3 — inside shifts flip their sign.

options.label: x = −3 and y = 2
options.feedback: The −2 outside is as-written: the horizontal asymptote sits at y = −2.

options.label: x = −2 and y = −3
options.feedback: Vertical tracks the denominator's zero (−3); horizontal tracks the outside shift (−2) — swapped here.

steps.body: Two guide rails: banned input (vertical), unreachable output (horizontal).
takeaways: Near the vertical asymptote outputs explode; far away they flatten.
Shifts move the asymptote pair exactly like a start point.
steps.teaser: Next: when a denominator zero is NOT an asymptote — holes.

concept.body: Feel the explosion: 1/x at x = 0.1, 0.01, 0.001 gives 10, 100, 1000. Smaller input, bigger output.

explanationVariants: Dividing 1 by a ten-times-smaller number gives a ten-times-bigger result.

commonErrors.feedback: Each factor of 10 smaller in x is a factor of 10 BIGGER in 1/x: 10000, one step past 1000.
